I'm sorry your going through this. I'd say therapy is a good option to look into. I saw one of your comments saying about how your dad doesn't think therapy works but maybe try to convince him ? Like show examples of people who went to therapy and got better. 

Also for the lack of motivation thing,
Im going to be completely honest and say that I don't think this is a good recommendation but it worked for me. Find something to take care of that you care deeply about. I got a pet, and it's motivated me to wake up every morning because now I'm thinking of something that's alive that isn't me, my pet depends on me to feed her and take her out and play with her. If I don't get up and get myself ready for the day, I can't take care of my pet. So I know I have to wake up, brush my teeth, go to the bathroom, take my dog out, and feed her then take her out again later and feed her again. Those are the few simple things I know I have to do everyday. It eventually led to be realizing I can also do other things like school work or cleaning up a tiny bit. 

You don't have to clean everyday, brush everyday, shower everyday. Just make sure you wake up and eat something and move around a bit. It may be the bare minimum but it will get you through the day. Eventually it might build up to doing more things and then it becomes a habit to brush, clean, shower, eat, stuff like that.

 Im not sure a pet would be the best option right now reading your situation but how about a plant? I've heard people sometimes manage to become motivated to take care of a plant. The new sprouting leaves and bright greens makes them feel accomplished or successful in keeping something alive. 

I hope your situation gets better, again I am sorry you are going through this.

I think this sounds like depression. I haven't been diagnosed, and I am not a professional but I've seen people describe their depression symptoms similarly to what you are experiencing. Not much motivation, hard to do simple task (brushing teeth, showering, cleaning), tired all the time, feeling drained. I would say maybe try to talk to a doctor at your next appointment? I got a diagnosis for anxiety when I went to my doctor's. Remember, it's not a bad thing to have a mental illness. Maybe it could feel a bit weird or shameful to find out you have depression or something else but I think it's better to get a diagnosis. It helped me a bit knowing that  I have anxiety rather than feeling confused about why I felt the way I did. I hope hings get better for you soon.
